llm.summary: This skill is a scoped report-writing assistant for teachers that discloses its use of student learning records and includes consent, aliasing, and manual-send safeguards.

dimensions.detail: Requested workspace fields are narrowly described for report generation, with schema scope limited to lesson logs, homework followups, course package data, parent communication summaries, student consent, and progress evidence.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is Markdown and JSON only; I found no executable scripts, remote payload retrieval, shell commands, credential handling, or install-time mutation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions require a specific student alias and explicit report or renewal intent before reading records, prohibit cross-student scans, and require authorization checks before parent-visible content.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can write progressEvidence entries, but reports themselves are not stored, writes are limited to confirmed stage evidence, deletion/status changes are explicitly delegated away, and pause/delete controls are documented.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill reads sensitive longitudinal student learning records and writes limited progress evidence, but that access is directly tied to generating stage and renewal reports and is repeatedly disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only in a teacher workspace where using student learning records for reports is intended. Teachers should verify the student alias and report type before generation, keep parent-visible output behind the documented consent checks, and localize the shared China-specific defaults before deploying in another region.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The description includes broad trigger examples, but the artifact also states that no workspace read occurs until a specific student alias is provided and the intent is report or renewal-related, so this is a bounded trigger-scoping note rather than a Review-level concern.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger table repeats generic examples, but line-level instructions require confirmation of the student and report type before reading any records and say ordinary chat should not run the report flow or write progressEvidence.
[SQP-3] expected: The Mainland China Chinese K12 defaults are a disclosed regional design constraint in shared platform conventions, not hidden behavior; operators outside that locale should localize safety channels, curriculum assumptions, and legal defaults before use.
